llm.summary: This is a coherent agent-identity template, but it gives the agent very broad autonomy and delegation authority without enough user control or data-scope limits.

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs use of sessions_send/sessions_spawn, shared-context files, and handoff messages containing relevant details, but it does not define data minimization, agent verification, workspace limits, or approval gates for non-financial external side effects.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown files only; I found no executable scripts, dependency installation, remote payload retrieval, or install-time commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SOUL.md uses active first-person authority, names Scott as the escalation target, requires delegation for tasks over 10 seconds, and says non-money actions should be done automatically, which is broader than a safe default approval boundary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: SOUL.md lists MEMORY.md curation as owned by the main session, which is disclosed, but it does not include a concrete hidden persistence mechanism or cross-session backdoor.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts match the stated purpose: a Pixel Familiar CEO/orchestrator identity with revenue goals, model routing, delegation, and operating rules.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you intentionally want an agent to operate as the Pixel Familiar CEO/orchestrator and to delegate work to named agents. Before use, tighten approval gates for file changes, deployments, external messages, account changes, sensitive data sharing, and memory updates, and require confirmation before forwarding context to other agents.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad autonomy rule is consistent with the autonomous CEO persona, but the artifact supports the concern because the approval boundary excludes only money, subscriptions, and cold outreach while allowing other sensitive actions without clear safeguards.
[T01] expected: The identity and delegation instructions are disclosed by SKILL.md rather than hidden, so I do not treat this as malicious hijacking; however, the active persona, external authority chain, and automatic delegation create a material review concern.
